title: Zero-worker fleets cannot refresh the delivery health they need to dispatch
problem_statement: delivery_health evidence has a single evidence_ttl_seconds (default 300) cache lifetime and is otherwise entirely demand-driven: a lane is only re-probed when something in the current cycle asks for it. Two demand sources existed before this task: idle_delivery_health_refresh_targets, which refreshes only the exact owner/reviewer already recorded on the canonical task row, and unavailable_assignment_fallback_refresh_targets, which does walk the configured worker_reassignment fallback chains but only once the incumbent is durably (terminally) unavailable -- a merely stale/expired ('unknown') probe is not terminal, so it never triggers that walk. plan_task_assignment_pair and worker_recovery_assignment_pair both search the same fallback chains for a viable owner/reviewer pair. With a live worker running, some other cycle eventually re-touches each candidate lane and this self-heals. With zero active workers, nothing else ever does: dispatch and worker-recovery retries keep reading the same expired evidence for the exact candidates they need, forever. This was reproduced live twice: a 13.6-hour zero-dispatch stall (2026-09-21T14:00Z to 2026-09-22T03:35Z) and a worker_recovery receipt stuck 'pending' for roughly 20 hours from 2026-09-22T04:44Z, both resolved only by an operator repeatedly driving 'supervisor.py --request-delivery-health-refresh' (which forces authorized_delivery_health_refresh_targets to probe every configured endpoint) until a probe happened to land inside the 5-minute TTL window a retry also ran in.

new_function_1.name: _demand_endpoint_health_refresh
new_function_1.purpose: Shared helper extracted from unavailable_assignment_fallback_refresh_targets's former inline demand_refresh closure: appends a due refresh target for one agent's endpoint(s) using the single shared health_gate_for_endpoint predicate. Pure refactor of existing logic, no behavior change; now shared by both unavailable_assignment_fallback_refresh_targets and the new zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets so a candidate's viability is judged by exactly one rule.

new_function_2.name: zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets
new_function_2.purpose: Demands a refresh for the same configured owner_fallbacks/reviewer_fallbacks chains unavailable_assignment_fallback_refresh_targets would eventually demand -- same probe budget, same health gate -- for every dispatch-ready task (todo/in_progress/review_approved/blocked, or in ready_dispatch.review_statuses) and every task fenced behind a pending worker-recovery receipt (task_has_pending_worker_recovery), but strictly only while live_total == 0. Returns [] immediately whenever any worker is active, so a running fleet gains zero extra probes from this path.
new_function_2.wired_into: build_dispatch_plan, between unavailable_assignment_fallback_refresh_targets and idle_delivery_health_refresh_targets in the refresh_targets assembly order.
new_function_2.revision_2026_09_23: Independent review of PR #5959 head ea39fdbfa9fb9c79251e6a62c7fccccdf8a1239f rejected the first cut of this function: its reviewer-side widening only walked reviewer_fallbacks rooted at the incumbent reviewer, but the real planners (plan_task_assignment_pair via reviewer_fallback_search_order, and worker_recovery_assignment_pair) also walk the reviewer fallback chain rooted at each *candidate owner* they consider, and worker_recovery_assignment_pair additionally seeds both its owner and reviewer searches from the pending receipt's 'previous' owner/reviewer (excluding the lost agent). A reviewer_fallbacks entry keyed on the candidate owner (for example Codex2 -> [Claude2], with no entry for the incumbent reviewer Claude) was therefore never discovered, leaving a viable (Codex2, Claude2) recovery pair self-locked behind stale Claude2 evidence. Fixed by: (1) resolving the pending receipt via _canonical_worker_recovery_receipt to read its previous owner/reviewer and lost worker agent; (2) seeding the owner-fallback walk from both the incumbent and previous owner, excluding the lost agent; (3) calling reviewer_fallback_search_order (the same shared traversal plan_task_assignment_pair uses) once for the incumbent owner and once for every discovered owner candidate, instead of a hand-rolled reviewer-fallbacks-from-incumbent-only walk; (4) adding a second reviewer-fallback walk seeded from the receipt's previous owner/reviewer for the worker_recovery reviewer-role case. The owner-side widening still excludes the incumbent reviewer from being probed as a speculative owner candidate (unchanged from the original cut) because plan_task_assignment_pair only ever reaches a non-incumbent owner candidate once the incumbent owner is not viable, and speculatively probing the reviewer's lane as a possible owner has no matching demand while the incumbent owner is healthy -- confirmed by the pre-existing test_idle_delivery_health_refresh_targets_filters_by_status_snapshot, which regressed and was restored by keeping that exclusion.

test_supervisor_py.revision_2026_09_23: test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_candidate_owner_reviewer_chain reproduces the exact isolated repro from the PR #5959 rejection: owner_fallbacks Codex->[Codex2], reviewer_fallbacks Codex2->[Claude2] (no chain rooted at the incumbent reviewer Claude), a pending owner-recovery receipt with previous owner/reviewer Codex/Claude and lost agent Codex, and Claude2 stale (expired). Asserts Claude2 is present in both the function's direct output and build_dispatch_plan's health_refresh_targets at live_total=0, and that the same setup yields zero targets at live_total=1.

docs_operations_auto_worker_readiness_md.change: New '### Delivery health refresh demand and the zero-worker self-lock' subsection documenting the demand-driven evidence model, the exact pre-existing gap (with function/line citations), and how zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets closes it, plus the same-cycle ordering between commit_delivery_health_observations and apply_post_dispatch_maintenance's second reconcile_pending_worker_recoveries pass.

ac1_self_triggered_refresh_no_operator_c.criterion: a cycle that finds ready work or a pending worker recovery receipt while zero workers are active refreshes the delivery health it needs without any operator command
ac1_self_triggered_refresh_no_operator_c.evidence: zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets walks the owner (and, for review-status/pending-recovery tasks, reviewer) fallback chains for every dispatch-ready task and every task with a pending worker-recovery receipt whenever live_total == 0, independent of request_delivery_health_refresh. As of the 2026-09-23 revision this reviewer-side walk reuses reviewer_fallback_search_order (the exact traversal plan_task_assignment_pair calls) once for the incumbent owner and once for every discovered owner-fallback candidate, and additionally seeds both the owner and reviewer walks from a pending recovery receipt's 'previous' owner/reviewer, excluding the lost agent -- closing the gap the independent review of PR #5959 (head ea39fdbfa9fb9c79251e6a62c7fccccdf8a1239f) found: a reviewer_fallbacks entry keyed only on a *candidate* owner (not the incumbent reviewer) was previously never reached. test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_pending_recovery_fallback, test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_ready_dispatch_owner_chain, and the new test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_candidate_owner_reviewer_chain (the exact deterministic isolated repro from the rejection) assert the targets are produced from build_dispatch_plan/the function directly with no Human/Ops request set.

ac2_stays_inside_probe_budget_never_prob.criterion: that self-triggered refresh stays inside the existing demand-driven probe budget and never probes providers that are already fresh
ac2_stays_inside_probe_budget_never_prob.evidence: The new demand is merged into the same refresh_targets list consumed by probe_demanded_delivery_health, which still applies delivery_health.refresh_max_per_cycle (unchanged, not widened). _demand_endpoint_health_refresh only appends a target when health_gate_for_endpoint (the same shared admission predicate) returns a non-None refresh target, i.e. the lane is not already healthy. test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_skips_already_fresh_candidates asserts an all-healthy fleet at live_total=0 yields zero targets.

ac3_retry_and_refresh_ordered_same_cycle.criterion: the recovery retry and the refresh are ordered so the retry evaluates evidence that is still valid in the same cycle
ac3_retry_and_refresh_ordered_same_cycle.evidence: commit_delivery_health_observations (supervisor.py, called from run_supervisor_cycle before apply_post_dispatch_maintenance) commits this cycle's freshly probed delivery_health before apply_post_dispatch_maintenance runs reconcile_runtime_on_boot -> reconcile_pending_worker_recoveries's second retry pass for the same cycle. The new demand target is folded into that same cycle's probe_targets by build_dispatch_plan before probe_demanded_delivery_health runs, so the second retry (after poll_workers_before_plan's earlier, pre-probe attempt) reads the just-refreshed evidence in the same cycle. No reordering of existing phases was needed or made; documented explicitly in auto-worker-readiness.md.

ac4_bounded_self_recovery.criterion: a fleet that reaches zero active workers with dispatchable work recovers on its own within a bounded number of cycles
ac4_bounded_self_recovery.evidence: Once zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets demands and probe_demanded_delivery_health refreshes the exact fallback candidate plan_task_assignment_pair/worker_recovery_assignment_pair need, the same-cycle retry (AC3) or the following cycle's planner pass finds a viable pair using fresh (non-expired) evidence, bounded by evidence_ttl_seconds and the existing per-cycle probe budget -- no unbounded wait on an external operator action remains. The 2026-09-23 revision closes the specific counterexample the PR #5959 review found deterministically: zero workers, owner_fallbacks Codex->[Codex2], reviewer_fallbacks Codex2->[Claude2] (no entry for the incumbent reviewer), a pending owner-recovery receipt for a lost Codex, Codex/Codex2 healthy, and only Claude2 stale. Before the fix, three build_dispatch_plan passes plus worker_recovery_assignment_pair all returned no viable pair because Claude2 was never demanded; test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_candidate_owner_reviewer_chain reproduces this exact configuration and asserts Claude2 is now demanded (and therefore refreshable) at live_total == 0, which is what lets worker_recovery_assignment_pair's reviewer-role search reach the (Codex2, Claude2) pair with fresh evidence.

ac5_regression_tests.criterion: regression tests cover the zero-worker plus pending-receipt case and prove no extra probes are issued while workers are running
ac5_regression_tests.evidence: test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_pending_recovery_fallback (zero workers + pending receipt -> fallback demand, including a build_dispatch_plan integration assertion), test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_noop_with_active_workers (live_total=1 -> targets == []), and the 2026-09-23 addition test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_candidate_owner_reviewer_chain (deterministic isolated repro of the PR #5959 rejection: candidate-owner-only reviewer_fallbacks entry plus receipt previous-owner/reviewer roots, asserted covered at live_total=0 and a no-op assertion at live_total=1) all added to .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py.

test_run_results.interpreter: .venv-pantheon/bin/python3 (Python 3.12, pytest; dependency interpreter inherited from the pre-provisioned worktree .venv-pantheon)
test_run_results.note: Full test_supervisor.py suite (386 tests including the 5 zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets tests) passes with no regressions after the 2026-09-23 fix. The revision initially regressed test_idle_delivery_health_refresh_targets_filters_by_status_snapshot by dropping the incumbent-reviewer exclusion from the owner-side fallback walk; restoring that exclusion (owner-side still excludes {owner, reviewer, lost_agent}, matching the original cut) fixed the regression without weakening the reviewer-side fix, since plan_task_assignment_pair only ever needs a non-incumbent owner candidate once the incumbent owner itself is not viable.

root_cause_analysis.why_idle_refresh_was_insufficient: idle_delivery_health_refresh_targets restricts its scan to 'active delivery lanes' derived from the canonical task row's own owner/reviewer fields (plus live workers and queued intents). It correctly refreshes the incumbent, but the incumbent is exactly the lane that is already known to be a dead end (a lost worker, or an owner the planner is trying to route around) -- it was never going to refresh the *replacement candidate's* lane.
root_cause_analysis.why_unavailable_assignment_fallback_refr: It walks owner_fallbacks/reviewer_fallbacks, but its trigger is assignment_terminal_unavailability(config, state, owner) returning non-None -- and that predicate explicitly treats a healthy, stale, or retryable endpoint as 'recoverable in place' (returns None), reserving a non-None terminal verdict for durable auth/quota/config failures only. A lane whose evidence simply expired past evidence_ttl_seconds is 'unknown', not terminal, so this scan stayed silent for exactly the case that matters once no worker is left to self-heal it.
root_cause_analysis.fix: zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets adds a third demand source that reuses the same configured fallback graph and the same shared health_gate_for_endpoint predicate (via the newly-extracted _demand_endpoint_health_refresh helper), but keys its trigger on live_total == 0 instead of on terminal-vs-stale classification. This is deliberately narrow: it changes nothing about how a running fleet behaves (the function is a no-op whenever live_total > 0), and it does not touch evidence_ttl_seconds, refresh_max_per_cycle, or any existing probe-budget policy per the task brief's explicit constraint not to widen the probe budget or remove the TTL.
root_cause_analysis.why_the_first_cut_still_self_locked: The first cut (PR #5959, rejected) walked reviewer_fallbacks rooted only at the incumbent reviewer, so a mapping entry keyed on a *candidate* owner (for example Codex2 -> [Claude2], with no entry for the incumbent reviewer Claude) was never discovered -- exactly the gap the independent review's deterministic isolated repro demonstrated. The real planners never had this limitation: plan_task_assignment_pair calls reviewer_fallback_search_order once per candidate owner it considers, and worker_recovery_assignment_pair additionally seeds both its owner and reviewer searches from the pending receipt's previous owner/reviewer. The 2026-09-23 revision makes zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets call the same reviewer_fallback_search_order helper per discovered owner candidate and resolve the receipt's previous owner/reviewer via _canonical_worker_recovery_receipt, instead of maintaining a second, narrower copy of that traversal.

review_notes_for_codex: The core fix is the new zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets function (supervisor.py) plus its one-line wiring into build_dispatch_plan; _demand_endpoint_health_refresh is a pure extraction of unavailable_assignment_fallback_refresh_targets's pre-existing inline closure with no behavior change (confirm via the unchanged unavailable_assignment_fallback_refresh_targets test coverage, which still passes untouched).

2026-09-23 (this revision, in response to the PR #5959 rejection): zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets's reviewer-side walk now calls the shared reviewer_fallback_search_order helper once for the incumbent owner and once for every owner-fallback candidate it discovers (instead of a hand-rolled walk rooted only at the incumbent reviewer), and resolves the pending worker-recovery receipt via _canonical_worker_recovery_receipt to also seed owner and reviewer walks from the receipt's previous owner/reviewer, excluding the lost agent -- reusing the exact same candidate-traversal logic plan_task_assignment_pair and worker_recovery_assignment_pair already use for the real reassignment decision, per the review's specific instruction not to hand-maintain a second copy of that traversal.

The owner-side walk deliberately still excludes the incumbent reviewer from being probed as a speculative owner candidate; removing that exclusion regressed test_idle_delivery_health_refresh_targets_filters_by_status_snapshot (a live, otherwise-healthy owner never actually reaches a fallback candidate in the real planner, so probing one preemptively is unbounded extra work with no matching demand) and was reverted. This is unchanged from the original PR #5959 cut; flagging for confirmation this restraint remains correct under review.

New test test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_candidate_owner_reviewer_chain reproduces the exact deterministic isolated counterexample from the rejection message (owner_fallbacks Codex->[Codex2], reviewer_fallbacks Codex2->[Claude2] only, pending owner-recovery receipt, Claude2 stale) and asserts it is now demanded at both the function level and through build_dispatch_plan, plus a live_total=1 no-op assertion for the probe-budget constraint (AC2).

AC3 (same-cycle ordering) required no code change: the existing phase ordering in run_supervisor_cycle already commits probe observations before apply_post_dispatch_maintenance's reconcile_pending_worker_recoveries pass. This was verified by reading the call sequence, not by a new test; flagging for independent confirmation during review.

docs/operations/auto-worker-readiness.md gained one new subsection documenting this exact mechanism with function/line citations, matching that document's existing precise citation style; no other claims in that document were changed by the original cut, and this revision does not add further doc changes beyond what is already there.

Live production recovery (evidence_ttl_seconds=300, the two real stalls cited in the task brief) is not independently re-reproduced here beyond the unit regression tests -- this is a supervisor-internal planning-logic fix verified at the unit level; a subsequent live dev-fleet observation window would be the natural follow-up if required.
